steps.note: Open the multi-stage event creation flow.
Enable the tenant behavior required for revision approval.
Provide the mandatory event title.
Create an RFQ-only event for the vendor revision scenario.
Apply an RFQ pricing template before adding items.
Add the product that will receive the bid.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet.
Commit a bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite the QA vendor who will submit and revise the bid.
Publish the RFQ so the vendor can bid.
Confirm the RFQ reached a real published project page.
Move to the separate vendor portal while keeping the buyer session available.
Open the event’s RFQ bid sheet as the invited vendor.
Submit Vendor A’s initial bid of 100.
Confirm the initial vendor bid was submitted.
Submit the vendor’s increase from 100 to 110, which should require buyer approval.

args.because: Your current bid is awaiting approval

steps.note: Verify a further revision is refused while the 110 increase is awaiting approval.
Return to the buyer’s console.
Open the RFQ Responses view where the pending revision is reviewed.
Confirm the buyer is offered approval for the pending revision.
Confirm the buyer is offered rejection for the pending revision.
Reject the pending 110 revision to verify the previous 100 bid remains current.
Confirm the current bid remains 100 after rejection.
Return to the vendor portal for a new revision after rejection.
Reopen the RFQ bid sheet for the vendor.
Submit the 110 revision again so the buyer can approve it.
Return to the buyer’s Responses view.
Reopen Responses to review the new pending revision.
Approve the vendor’s 110 revision.
Confirm 110 becomes the current bid after approval.
